not_available.mobot_cultivars: MOBOT also lists Gaillardia aristata 'Bijou' (taxonid 249992) and BARBICAN YELLOW RED RING (445827), plus G. × grandiflora (263710) and cultivars; not extracted — species page only
not_available.rhs_cultivars: RHS also has G. aristata 'Maxima Aurea' (152412), 'Lucky Wheeler' (333428), 'Gaiz0005' (357631) and many G. × grandiflora pages; only the species page (67388) extracted
not_available.usda_plant_guide: USDA NRCS Plant Guide pg_gaar.pdf exists (public domain) but was not read — the brief limits USDA extraction to the PLANTS API profile and characteristics
not_available.kpu: KPU plant database lists only 'Gaillardia cvs.' (/Plant/gagr), no species page; tier C, link only

external_refs.kpu_note: KPU entry is 'Gaillardia cvs.' (cultivar group), not the species

entity_facts.synonyms_note: none listed by RHS, E-Flora BC or USDA PLANTS (HasSynonyms false); the garden hybrid Gaillardia × grandiflora (G. aristata × G. pulchella) is a different taxon and was not substituted
entity_facts.common_name_note: USDA: blanketflower, common gaillardia; RHS: common gaillardia; E-Flora BC: brown-eyed Susan (common gaillardia); MOBOT: blanket flower
entity_facts.botanical_growth_form: clump-forming herbaceous perennial from a slender taproot, 20–70 cm (E-Flora), hairy stems and lance-shaped grey-green leaves (RHS, MOBOT)
entity_facts.kpu_plant_type_note: RHS and MOBOT both type it 'Herbaceous perennial'; USDA 'Forb/herb', duration perennial, leaf retention no
entity_facts.origin: western North America: BC and the Prairie provinces east to Manitoba, south to Colorado, Utah, California and northern Oregon (E-Flora, MOBOT); native in Canada and the lower 48 states (USDA)
entity_facts.bc_native_range_note: E-Flora BC: common in south-central and south-eastern BC (interior; modal BEC zone IDF, also BG and PP; no CWH or CDF stations); introduced in south-western BC (lower Fraser Valley). So BC sources treat it as native to the interior only, NOT native west of the Cascades / in the Vancouver region — any 'Native planting' landscape use in Vancouver should be read as regionally (not locally) native
entity_facts.companions_note: no source names a specific companion species
